title: Consumer classification contract
lead: Document and test the descriptor members a downstream classifier relies on to match delimited lab exports against its own declared file types, so a consumer can swap its stand-in describer for squalify. **Not in this slice:** classification itself (a non-goal), new descriptor members unless a gap is found.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A first consumer (a splitter for lab sweep tables, in another repo) now reads files as describe, classify, transform, split. It ships a small stand-in describer whose output is a subset of this descriptor and will replace it with squalify once delimited profiling exists. Its classifier needs a stable, documented subset; squalify still only describes.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `docs/descriptor.md`: a "Consumer subset" section listing the members and their stability under the schema-version policy
- tests on synthetic fixtures under `tests/` (no real files); the private-corpus harness (sq-18) covers real files

- Owner decisions (2026-10-27, review): (1) A change to the null vocabulary or the unit table bumps only `limits.nullTokens` / `limits.unitTable`, not `schemaVersion`; consumers pin those table versions alongside `schemaVersion`, and the Consumer subset says so. (2) Today's ragged-record-at-run-start behaviour is documented as a known limitation, with a pointer to the new ragged-run-start item.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A synthetic lab sweep table (key columns with an `(id)` unit, `(unit)` measurement columns, unitless setup columns, interleaved all-null separator rows) gives: the dialect and header (sq-04), every header name with its parsed unit convention (sq-14), the row classes with the all-null class (sq-17), and per field `type`, `nulls` and `constant` (sq-05).
- A synthetic one-condition capture table (no key columns, a few varying columns, the rest constant) gives `constant` true for the constant fields and false for the varying ones.
- With values off, a constant field's description says it is constant without revealing the value (`statsWithheld`).
- The consumer-subset members are byte-identical across two runs.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: - Document how `constant` treats nulls (every non-null value equal) and how a consumer derives "constant with NULL counted as a value" from `constant`, `nulls` and `count`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Build, test and format pass; `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: The owner commits. Do not commit; never add Co-Authored-By or similar lines.
